Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 3-day history of new, severe, diffuse headache worst over right eye, photophobia, visual “shooting lights,” mild nausea, partial NSAID response.  
• No focal neurologic deficits, no fever, no meningism.  
• Likely primary migraine with visual aura given features and maternal history.  
• Red-flag considerations discussed: cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, idiopathic intracranial hypertension; require examination and possible further work-up.  
• Plan:  
  – Arrange urgent face-to-face appointment for full neurological exam and fundoscopy; check blood pressure.  
  – Prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) plus paracetamol as adjunct; advise taking with food.  
  – Continue current OCP for now; may need change if migraine with aura confirmed.  
  – Safety-net: attend emergency department if headache worsens, changes character, or new symptoms develop.  
  – Patient to monitor and record symptom pattern.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Migraine with visual aura – High likelihood: unilateral severe pain, photophobia, visual phenomena, family history, partial NSAID response.  
2. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Moderate likelihood: female on estrogen OCP, persistent headache, positional component; no neuro deficits yet.  
3. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension – Moderate likelihood: young woman with visual disturbance; needs optic-disc assessment; fewer classic features present.
